provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Pencil grip refresh
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to hold pencil correctly.
The pupils should be able to write with control.
Introduction:
We use pencils to write. Last term we learned to hold pencils.
Content:
Hold pencil with three fingers. Thumb, pointer and middle finger. Rest pencil on your ring finger. Make a duck mouth with your fingers. Practice making small circles. Pretend to write your name.
Class activity:
Pencil grip relay. Pass a pencil with correct grip. First group to finish wins.
Evaluation questions:
Show me how to hold a pencil. Which finger is on top? What shape does the grip make?
Summary:
Good grip helps us write well.

topics.title: Letter families 1
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify letter family members.
The pupils should be able to write letters c, a, d, g, o, q.
Introduction:
Letters are like families. Some letters look alike. We learned some letters last term.
Content:
The c family has c, a, d, g, o, q. Start with c shape. Add a line for a. Add a bump for d. Add a tail for g. Make a full circle for o. Add a tail for q. Write them in rows. Start at the top.
Class activity:
Letter family hopscotch. Draw letters on floor. Jump on each letter as you say its name.
Evaluation questions:
Which letter is in the c family? How do you write letter d? What comes after o in this family?
Summary:
The c family letters start the same way.

topics.title: Letter families 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify letter family members.
The pupils should be able to write letters l, t, i, u, y.
Introduction:
We have another letter family. These letters are tall and straight. Some have dots or little lines.
Content:
The l family has l, t, i, u, y. Start with a tall line down for l. Add a cross on top for t. Add a dot for i. Add a curve for u. Add two lines for y. Write them in rows. Keep them tall and neat.
Class activity:
Letter family parade. Hold arm straight up for l. Make cross with arms for t. Point finger for i. Curve arm for u. Make V with arms for y.
Evaluation questions:
Which letter has a dot? How do you write letter u? What shape is letter y?
Summary:
The l family letters have straight lines.

topics.title: Letter families 3
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify letter family members.
The pupils should be able to write letters r, n, m, h, b, p.
Introduction:
Today we meet the r family. These letters have curves and bumps. Some are tall and some are small.
Content:
The r family has r, n, m, h, b, p. Start with a curve for r. Add a hump for n. Add two humps for m. Add a tall line for h. Add a tummy for b. Add a round tummy for p. Write them in rows. Keep the humps the same size.
Class activity:
Letter family dance. Move in curves like r. Hop for n. Bounce for m. Stand tall for h. Pat tummy for b. Spin for p.
Evaluation questions:
Which letter has two humps? How do you write letter b? What comes after m in this family?
Summary:
The r family letters have curves and humps.

topics.title: Words 1
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to read simple words.
The pupils should be able to write words cat, dog, sun, hat.
Introduction:
Letters make words. We can read words. Words tell us things. Like our names.
Content:
Cat has c - a - t. A cat says meow. Dog has d - o - g. A dog says woof. Sun has s - u - n. The sun is hot. Hat has h - a - t. We wear hats in sun. Write each word three times. Use finger spaces.
Class activity:
Word picture match. Draw pictures of cat, dog, sun, hat. Match to written words.
Evaluation questions:
How do you write cat? What does dog say? Which word is hot?
Summary:
We can read and write simple words.

topics.title: Words 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to read simple words.
The pupils should be able to write words hand, milk, ball, star.
Introduction:
More words to learn! We use these words every day. Like when we eat or play.
Content:
Hand has h - a - n - d. We have two hands. Milk has m - i - l - k. We drink milk. Ball has b - a - l - l. We play with ball. Star has s - t - a - r. Stars twinkle at night. Write words on lines. Keep letters small.
Class activity:
Word building game. Use letter cards to make hand, milk, ball, star.
Evaluation questions:
How do you write milk? What do we play with? Which word has five letters?
Summary:
We can write more words now.

topics.title: Sentences 1
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write simple sentences.
The pupils should be able to use finger spaces and full stops.
Introduction:
Words make sentences. Sentences tell us more. Like when we tell a story.
Content:
The cat is fat. This is a sentence. Use finger spaces between words. Put a full stop at the end. Full stop looks like a dot. Write the sentence three times. Start with capital letter.
Class activity:
Sentence building. Use word cards to make The cat is fat. Add full stop card at end.
Evaluation questions:
Where do we put finger spaces? What does a full stop look like? How do we start a sentence?
Summary:
Sentences have spaces and full stops.

topics.title: Numbers 1 to 20
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify numbers 1 to 20.
The pupils should be able to write numbers 1 to 20 neatly.
Introduction:
Numbers are everywhere. We count with numbers. Like when we count our fingers.
Content:
Write numbers 1 to 20 in rows. 1 is a straight line. 2 has a curve and line. 3 has two curves. 4 has points. 5 has a belly. 6 has a circle. 7 has a line and slash. 8 has two circles. 9 has a circle and line. 10 has a one and zero. Keep numbers small and neat.
Class activity:
Number hop. Write numbers on floor. Jump on each number as you count.
Evaluation questions:
How do you write number 5? Which number comes after 7? What does number 8 look like?
Summary:
We can write numbers 1 to 20.

topics.title: Numbers 21 to 50
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify numbers 21 to 50.
The pupils should be able to write numbers 21 to 50 neatly.
Introduction:
We know numbers up to 20. Now we learn more numbers. Like when we count money.
Content:
Write numbers 21 to 50 in rows. 20 has a two and zero. 21 has a two and one. 30 has a three and zero. Count by tens. 40 has a four and zero. 50 has a five and zero. 50 is our champion number. Keep tens neat.
Class activity:
Number line game. Make a number line on floor. Jump and count from 21 to 50.
Evaluation questions:
How do you write number 30? What comes after 29? Which number has a five and zero?
Summary:
We can write numbers up to 50.

topics.title: Revision and best page
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to show their best handwriting.
The pupils should be able to identify good handwriting.
Introduction:
We learned many things. Letters, words, sentences, numbers. Now we choose our best work.
Content:
Look at all your pages. Find your best handwriting. It could be letters, words or numbers. Make your handwriting neat. Letters should be the same size. Spaces should be even. Numbers should be clear. Your best page goes on the wall.
Class activity:
Handwriting wall of fame. Display best pages. Class votes for neatest handwriting.
Evaluation questions:
What makes good handwriting? Which page is your best? Why is it your best?
Summary:
We all have good handwriting.
